title: The Life of Lawrence of Arabia
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 推出的 English Learning for Curious Minds。在这个节目中，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事，了解世界上各种奇妙的事物，一边提高英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today, is the start of yet another three-part mini-series.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们将开启又一个三集系列节目。

sentences.en: This one is on the topic of World War I.
sentences.zh: 这一系列的主题是第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: But we aren’t really going to talk all that much about World War I, at least not directly.
sentences.zh: 但我们并不会过多地谈论一战本身，至少不会直接谈论。

sentences.en: Instead, we are going to explore this period through the lives of unusual characters involved in the war, some more directly than others.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们将通过参与战争的几位不寻常人物的生平来探索这段时期，他们中有些人的参与程度比其他人更直接。

sentences.en: So, in today’s episode, part one, we are going to talk about the amazing story of T.E.
sentences.zh: 在今天的第一集里，我们要聊聊 T.E. 的传奇故事。

sentences.en: Lawrence, the British archaeologist and army officer who fought alongside Arabian tribesmen for a united Arab nation, all while harbouring a guilty secret.
sentences.zh: Lawrence，这位英国考古学家兼军官曾与阿拉伯部落并肩作战，为建立一个统一的阿拉伯国家而奋斗，同时内心还隐藏着一个令他愧疚的秘密。

sentences.en: Next up, in part two, we’ll learn about the story of Mata Hari, the Dutch woman who became an exotic dancer and the talk of Paris, before being executed by a firing squad on the charge of being a spy.
sentences.zh: 接下来，在第二集中，我们将了解 Mata Hari 的故事。这位荷兰女性成为了充满异国情调的舞者，名震巴黎，最后却因间谍罪被行刑队处决。

sentences.en: And in part three, in the interests of balance, we will talk about Manfred von Richthofen, a German aircraft pilot so deadly he was known to his enemies as “The Red Baron”.
sentences.zh: 在第三集中，为了平衡起见，我们将聊聊 Manfred von Richthofen。他是一位极其致命的德国飞行员，被敌人称为“红男爵”。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and learn about the unlikely life of T.E.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们直接进入正题，了解 T.E. 那段不可思议的人生。

sentences.en: Lawrence.
sentences.zh: Lawrence。

sentences.en: A title you will often find in lists of “The Greatest Films Ever Made” is the 1962 classic “Lawrence of Arabia”.
sentences.zh: 在“影史最伟大电影”的榜单中，你经常会看到 1962 年的经典影片 Lawrence of Arabia。

sentences.en: The trailer for the film opens with wide-angle shots of a man trekking through a vast desert on a camel.
sentences.zh: 电影预告片以广角镜头开场，画面中一个男人骑着骆驼穿行在广袤的沙漠中。

sentences.en: As the camel obediently plods forward, putting one foot in front of the other in the scorching desert sand, you hear the words of the narrator, ostensibly about the man on the camel.
sentences.zh: 随着骆驼在滚烫的沙漠中顺从地一步步向前挪动，你会听到旁白的声音，表面上是在谈论骆驼上的那个男人。

sentences.en: He says, “I deem him one of the greatest beings alive in our time.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我认为他是我们这个时代最伟大的生命之一。

sentences.en: His name will live in history. It will live in the annals of war…it will live in the legends of Arabia.”
sentences.zh: 他的名字将名垂青史。它将载入战争史册……它将流传在阿拉伯的传说中。”

sentences.en: The quote is attributed to Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 这句话出自 Winston Churchill。

sentences.en: Immediately, the viewer is hooked. If Churchill, the great wartime leader, is calling this man “one of the greatest beings alive in our time”, well, that certainly is something.
sentences.zh: 观众立刻被吸引住了。如果伟大的战时领袖 Churchill 都称此人为“我们时代最伟大的生命之一”，那他确实非同凡响。

sentences.en: The trailer continues, with the narrator going on to say that “no man of our time has drawn upon himself so much praise and so much criticism”.
sentences.zh: 预告片继续，旁白接着说道：“我们这个时代，没有哪个人像他这样赢得了如此多的赞誉，也招致了如此多的批评。”

sentences.en: It is a fair assessment, but now we must move from talking about the movie to the real man.
sentences.zh: 这是一个公正的评价，但现在我们必须从电影转向现实中的那个人。

sentences.en: Thomas Edward Lawrence was born in 1888 in north Wales, the second of five sons.
sentences.zh: Thomas Edward Lawrence 1888 年出生于北威尔士，在五个儿子中排行老二。

sentences.en: He was a shy but passionate boy. When he set his mind to something, he did it.
sentences.zh: 他是一个害羞但充满热情的男孩。一旦他下定决心做某事，就一定会做到。

sentences.en: And from an early age he was passionate about history.
sentences.zh: 他从小就对历史充满热情。

sentences.en: When he was 15, he spent the summer cycling around a large area of southern England with a friend, visiting every single church he came across.
sentences.zh: 15 岁那年，他花了一个夏天的时间和朋友一起骑自行车游历了英格兰南部的大片地区，参观了沿途遇到的每一座教堂。

sentences.en: The boys took notes, made rubbings of brass memorials, and when they had finished, they presented their findings to the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford.
sentences.zh: 孩子们做了笔记，拓印了黄铜纪念碑，结束后，他们将研究成果提交给了牛津大学的 Ashmolean Museum。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, the museum’s curators were astounded and impressed by the boys’ attention to detail.
sentences.zh: 正如你所料，博物馆的馆长们对这些孩子对细节的关注感到震惊并留下了深刻印象。

sentences.en: And this wasn’t a one-off. The teenage boy had got the bug, he had had a small taste of adventure.
sentences.zh: 这并非偶然。这个少年已经迷上了这件事，他初尝了冒险的滋味。

sentences.en: Later that summer, he cycled around France on his own, visiting medieval castles and taking notes.
sentences.zh: 那个夏天晚些时候，他独自骑车环游法国，参观中世纪城堡并做笔记。

sentences.en: Then he did the same thing again the following summer, still aged only 16.
sentences.zh: 第二年夏天，他再次故技重施，当时他才 16 岁。

sentences.en: This clear passion for understanding the past earned him a place at Oxford University, where he read history, and for his thesis, he went one step further.
sentences.zh: 这种对了解过去的明确热情让他获得了 Oxford University 的席位，他在那里攻读历史，为了完成论文，他更进一步。

sentences.en: In his last year at university, and aged only 20, he embarked on a three-month trip to Syria to study castles of the crusader era, so medieval castles.
sentences.zh: 在大学最后一年，年仅 20 岁的他踏上了为期三个月的叙利亚之旅，去研究十字军时期的城堡，也就是中世纪城堡。

sentences.en: Now, even putting aside the more recent political instability in the region, even in the 21st century, Syria is not the easiest country to get around.
sentences.zh: 即使撇开该地区近期的政治动荡不谈，即便是在 21 世纪，叙利亚也不是一个容易周游的国家。

sentences.en: But Lawrence visited in 1909, and he was going from abandoned castle to abandoned castle.
sentences.zh: 但 Lawrence 是在 1909 年访问的，他当时穿梭于一座又一座废弃的城堡之间。

sentences.en: There was practically no infrastructure, no way of getting from one castle to the next.
sentences.zh: 那里几乎没有基础设施，没有从一座城堡到下一座城堡的交通方式。

sentences.en: So…he mostly walked and rode on donkeys, claiming to have travelled a grand total of 1,600 kilometres.
sentences.zh: 所以……他大部分时间是步行或骑驴，声称总共旅行了 1600 公里。

sentences.en: He had already developed a keen interest in the Middle East, but this trip really took it to a new level.
sentences.zh: 他已经对中东产生了浓厚的兴趣，而这次旅行真正将这种兴趣提升到了一个新的高度。

sentences.en: And this area, I should add, was still part of the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，当时这个地区仍然是 Ottoman Empire 的一部分。

sentences.en: There was no Syria, no Lebanon, no Jordan, this was all part of the sprawling Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 当时还没有叙利亚、黎巴嫩或约旦，这些都是庞大的 Ottoman Empire 的一部分。

sentences.en: And this will be of vital importance to the rest of our story.
sentences.zh: 这对我们接下来的故事至关重要。

sentences.en: So, in 1910, at the age of 22, Thomas Lawrence graduated, and like any fresh graduate, he was in the market for a job.
sentences.zh: 1910 年，22 岁的 Thomas Lawrence 毕业了，像任何应届毕业生一样，他开始找工作。

sentences.en: Clearly not any job, though. It would have to involve some form of exploring the past, preferably in the Middle East.
sentences.zh: 显然不是随便什么工作。它必须涉及某种形式的探索过去，最好是在中东。

sentences.en: And sure enough, he did not become a lawyer or an accountant; he found a job as an archaeologist.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，他没有成为律师或会计师，而是找到了一份考古学家的工作。

sentences.en: He worked across the Middle East, in modern-day Lebanon, Syria, Israel and Egypt.
sentences.zh: 他的足迹遍布中东，包括今天的黎巴嫩、叙利亚、以色列和埃及。

sentences.en: And he seemed different from most of the other Western archaeologists exploring the area.
sentences.zh: 他似乎与在该地区探索的大多数其他西方考古学家不同。

sentences.en: He studied Arabic, and spoke it practically fluently.
sentences.zh: 他学习了阿拉伯语，而且说得几乎非常流利。

sentences.en: He was actually interested in the language and culture of the people living there, whereas most of his fellow archaeologists believed they were there to teach; there was nothing they could learn from these backwards “desert people”.
sentences.zh: 他对当地人的语言和文化真正感兴趣，而他的大多数考古学家同行认为他们是去教化的；他们觉得从这些落后的“沙漠民族”身上学不到任何东西。

sentences.en: Now, fast forward to 1914. The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria, in the now Bosnian capital of Sarajevo, had ripple effects that extended all the way to the Arabian desert.
sentences.zh: 现在，时间快进到 1914 年。奥地利大公 Franz Ferdinand 在现在的波斯尼亚首都萨拉热窝遇刺，其连锁反应一直延伸到了阿拉伯沙漠。

sentences.en: As you may know, or remember from our last mini-series on the theme of the fall of the Ottoman Empire, the Ottomans sided with Germany.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能知道的，或者记得我们上一期关于 Ottoman Empire 衰落主题的系列节目，奥斯曼人站在了德国一边。

sentences.en: Suddenly, this vast swathe of territory in the Middle East was the enemy.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，中东这片广袤的土地成了敌占区。

sentences.en: Lawrence was sent to Egypt, which was under the rule of the British at the time, where he was tasked with making sense of what was going on in the region.
sentences.zh: Lawrence 被派往当时受英国统治的埃及，任务是弄清楚该地区发生了什么。

sentences.en: He was, in many ways, the perfect man for the job.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，他都是这份工作的最佳人选。

sentences.en: He spoke Arabic, he understood local customs and traditions, and he felt more at home in the Middle East than he did back in England.
sentences.zh: 他会说阿拉伯语，了解当地的习俗和传统，而且他在中东比在英国老家感觉更自在。

sentences.en: But at this stage, Lawrence was not yet a hero, not yet the legendary “Lawrence of Arabia.”
sentences.zh: 但在这个阶段，Lawrence 还不是英雄，还不是传奇的 Lawrence of Arabia。

sentences.en: He was simply a junior intelligence officer, working behind the scenes in Cairo, reading reports, interrogating prisoners, and trying to make sense of the complex tribal and political landscape of the region.
sentences.zh: 他只是开罗的一名初级情报官员，在幕后工作，阅读报告、审讯囚犯，并试图理清该地区复杂的部落和政治格局。

sentences.en: And it was complex. The Ottoman Empire ruled over the Middle East, but its control was not absolute.
sentences.zh: 确实很复杂。Ottoman Empire 统治着中东，但其控制力并非绝对。

sentences.en: In the deserts of Arabia, tribal leaders held enormous power, often ruling over their lands with little direct interference from Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉伯沙漠中，部落领袖拥有巨大的权力，通常统治着自己的土地，很少受到来自君士坦丁堡的直接干预。

sentences.en: The British, who were desperate to weaken the Ottoman position, saw an opportunity: if they could convince the Arab tribes to rise up against their Ottoman rulers, it would divide the enemy’s forces and stretch their resources thin.
sentences.zh: 迫切希望削弱奥斯曼地位的英国人看到了一个机会：如果他们能说服阿拉伯部落反抗奥斯曼统治者，就能分散敌人的兵力并耗尽他们的资源。

sentences.en: The man at the centre of this idea was Sharif Hussein of Mecca, the ruler of the Hejaz, a region that included the two holiest cities in Islam—Mecca and Medina.
sentences.zh: 这一构想的核心人物是麦卡的 Sharif Hussein，他是汉志地区的统治者，该地区包括伊斯兰教最神圣的两座城市——麦加和麦地那。

sentences.en: Hussein had grown increasingly wary of Ottoman rule and had ambitions of establishing an independent Arab kingdom.
sentences.zh: Hussein 对奥斯曼的统治越来越警惕，并怀有建立独立阿拉伯王国的野心。

sentences.en: And the British promised him exactly that, if he could overthrow the Ottomans, that was.
sentences.zh: 英国人正是这样向他承诺的，前提是他能推翻奥斯曼人。

sentences.en: In 1915, there was a series of letters exchanged between Sharif Hussein and the British High Commissioner in Egypt, Henry McMahon.
sentences.zh: 1915 年，Sharif Hussein 与英国驻埃及高级专员 Henry McMahon 之间进行了一系列书信往来。

sentences.en: In these letters, McMahon seemed to confirm that if the Arabs helped to overthrow the Ottomans, they would be granted their own independent state.
sentences.zh: 在这些信件中，McMahon 似乎确认，如果阿拉伯人帮助推翻奥斯曼人，他们将被授予建立独立国家的权利。

sentences.en: And so, it began. In 1916, Hussein’s forces, led in large part by his son Prince Faisal, launched attacks against Ottoman garrisons.
sentences.zh: 于是，行动开始了。1916 年，Hussein 的军队在很大程度上由他的儿子 Prince Faisal 领导，开始向奥斯曼驻军发起进攻。

sentences.en: But it was not a smooth campaign. The Arab forces were desert warriors, skilled at a certain type of warfare, where horses and swords were involved, but they were bitterly unprepared for a war fought by machine guns and artillery.
sentences.zh: 但这场战役并不顺利。阿拉伯军队是沙漠战士，擅长某种涉及马匹和长剑的战争，但对于机关枪和火炮构成的战争，他们完全没有准备。

sentences.en: What’s more, they lacked unity. Many tribes were reluctant to join the revolt, suspicious of British intentions or unwilling to commit without clear guarantees of victory.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们缺乏团结。许多部落不愿加入起义，要么怀疑英国人的意图，要么在没有明确获胜保证的情况下不愿投入战斗。

sentences.en: This was where Lawrence entered the picture.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Lawrence 登场的地方。

sentences.en: By this point, he had itchy feet from sitting at his relatively cushy Cairo desk job.
sentences.zh: 此时，他已经厌倦了在开罗那份相对安逸的案头工作，渴望行动。

sentences.en: Two of his younger brothers had been killed in the bloody battlefields of northern France, and he felt a deep sense of guilt that he hadn’t really done anything.
sentences.zh: 他的两个弟弟在法国北部血腥的战场上牺牲了，他因为自己没能真正做点什么而感到深深的愧疚。

sentences.en: He was ready, and he jumped at the opportunity to get closer to the action.
sentences.zh: 他准备好了，并抓住机会去亲临前线。

sentences.en: He was sent from Cairo to meet Prince Faisal in person, to assess the situation and determine how Britain could best support the Arab fighters.
sentences.zh: 他被从开罗派去亲自会见 Prince Faisal，以评估局势并确定英国如何能最好地支持阿拉伯战士。

sentences.en: What he found was a movement that was full of ambition but lacking a defined strategy.
sentences.zh: 他发现这是一场充满雄心但缺乏明确战略的运动。

sentences.en: The Arab forces had the advantage of mobility, knowledge of the terrain, and motivation, but they lacked the heavy weaponry, discipline, and resources of the Ottoman army.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯军队拥有机动性、地形知识和动力等优势，但缺乏奥斯曼军队那样的重型武器、纪律和资源。

sentences.en: Lawrence believed the Arabs needed a new way of fighting.
sentences.zh: Lawrence 认为阿拉伯人需要一种新的战斗方式。

sentences.en: They could not win a conventional war against the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 他们无法在常规战争中战胜奥斯曼人。

sentences.en: They didn’t have the numbers or the weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们没有足够的人数或武器。

sentences.en: Instead, they needed to wage guerrilla warfare—hit-and-run attacks, sabotage and psychological pressure.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们需要进行游击战——游击袭击、破坏和心理压力。

sentences.en: Rather than trying to hold and defend territory, they would move like the desert itself, appearing suddenly, striking hard, and disappearing before the enemy could retaliate.
sentences.zh: 他们不应试图占领和保卫领土，而应像沙漠本身一样移动，突然出现，猛烈打击，并在敌人反击前消失。

sentences.en: Faisal listened. He seemed to understand that Lawrence, unlike most of his fellow British officers, was not trying to command the Arabs but rather to advise them in their own fight.
sentences.zh: Prince Faisal 听进去了。他似乎明白，Lawrence 与大多数英国军官不同，他不是想指挥阿拉伯人，而是在他们自己的战斗中提供建议。

sentences.en: A strange friendship developed between the British officer and the Arab prince—two men from entirely different worlds, but seemingly united by a shared vision of Arab independence.
sentences.zh: 这位英国军官和这位阿拉伯王子之间建立了一种奇特的友谊——两个来自完全不同世界的人，似乎因为对阿拉伯独立的共同愿景而团结在一起。

sentences.en: Lawrence abandoned his British uniform, and instead dressed in flowing white robes like an Arab sheikh.
sentences.zh: Lawrence 脱下了他的英国制服，换上了像阿拉伯酋长那样飘逸的白袍。

sentences.en: It was partly practicality—the robes were more suited to the desert—but it was also a symbol.
sentences.zh: 这部分是出于实用性——长袍更适合沙漠——但也是一种象征。

sentences.en: He was not just an outsider observing the revolt.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是一个观察起义的局外人。

sentences.en: He was part of it. He fought alongside the Arab soldiers, not just hanging back sipping tea and advising the prince, but on the frontlines, leading guerilla missions, setting off explosives, and getting involved in a far more active way than he was meant to.
sentences.zh: 他是其中的一员。他与阿拉伯士兵并肩作战，不只是躲在后面喝茶给王子出主意，而是身处前线，领导游击任务，引爆炸药，以一种远超他职责范围的积极方式参与其中。

sentences.en: Remember, he had been sent to be an informal advisor to the prince; he hadn’t been sent to fight.
sentences.zh: 记住，他被派去是担任王子的非正式顾问；他并不是被派去打仗的。

sentences.en: And although he wasn’t a soldier by training, he seemed to have a natural sense of military strategy.
sentences.zh: 尽管他没有受过正规的士兵训练，但他似乎天生就有军事战略头脑。

sentences.en: Perhaps the most famous example of this was with Aqaba.
sentences.zh: 也许最著名的例子就是阿卡巴。

sentences.en: The port of Aqaba, on the Red Sea, was a vital Ottoman stronghold.
sentences.zh: 红海沿岸的阿卡巴港是奥斯曼帝国的重要据点。

sentences.en: It was heavily defended from the sea, where the Ottomans expected any attack to come.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼人预料攻击会来自海上，因此在海防方面戒备森严。

sentences.en: But Lawrence had a different plan. Instead of attacking from the water, he proposed an impossible route—crossing the deadly Nefud Desert and attacking Aqaba from behind.
sentences.zh: 但 Lawrence 有一个不同的计划。他没有从水路进攻，而是提出了一条不可能的路线——穿越致命的内夫得沙漠并从后方袭击阿卡巴。

sentences.en: The journey was brutal. Lawrence, Faisal’s fighters, and the fearsome Bedouin cavalry, led by a fierce warrior named Auda abu Tayi, crossed nearly 1000 kilometres of some of the harshest terrain on Earth, suffering from thirst, exhaustion, and the relentless heat.
sentences.zh: 旅程非常残酷。Lawrence、Prince Faisal 的战士们以及由勇猛战士 Auda abu Tayi 领导的可怕的贝都因骑兵，穿越了地球上近 1000 公里最恶劣的地形，忍受着干渴、疲惫和无情的酷热。

sentences.en: When they finally reached Aqaba in July of 1917, coming from the desert in the north rather than by sea in the south, they took the Ottoman defenders by surprise.
sentences.zh: 当他们最终在 1917 年 7 月到达阿卡巴时，他们是从北部的沙漠而不是南部的海面攻入的，这让奥斯曼守军措手不及。

sentences.en: The garrison collapsed. Some defenders fled into the sea in panic.
sentences.zh: 驻军溃败了。一些守军惊慌失措地逃入海中。

sentences.en: It was a stunning victory. Aqaba was a turning point.
sentences.zh: 这是一场惊人的胜利。阿卡巴是一个转折点。

sentences.en: It gave the Arab forces a port for supplies, a symbolic victory, and credibility on the world stage.
sentences.zh: 它为阿拉伯军队提供了一个补给港口，一场象征性的胜利，以及在世界舞台上的信誉。

sentences.en: Lawrence rode for days through the desert to deliver the news to British commanders in Cairo.
sentences.zh: Lawrence 骑马在沙漠中奔波了数日，将消息传达给开罗的英国指挥官。

sentences.en: He arrived, sunburned, half-starved, and covered in dust, but triumphant.
sentences.zh: 他到达时，皮肤被晒伤，半饥半饱，满身尘土，但凯旋而归。

sentences.en: However, the war was not over. After Aqaba, Lawrence and the Arab forces turned their focus to the Hejaz Railway, which was the lifeline of the Ottoman forces in the region.
sentences.zh: 然而，战争并未结束。阿卡巴之后，Lawrence 和阿拉伯军队将注意力转向了汉志铁路，那是该地区奥斯曼军队的生命线。

sentences.en: Instead of trying to capture cities, they attacked the railway itself, derailing trains, blowing up bridges, and planting mines.
sentences.zh: 他们没有试图夺取城市，而是攻击铁路本身，使火车脱轨、炸毁桥梁并埋设地雷。

sentences.en: It was a war of sabotage. The Ottomans could never be sure where the next attack would come.
sentences.zh: 这是一场破坏战。奥斯曼人永远无法确定下一次袭击会来自何处。

sentences.en: And it was during one of these missions that Lawrence experienced the darkest moment of his life.
sentences.zh: 正是在其中一次任务中，Lawrence 经历了人生中最黑暗的时刻。

sentences.en: In late 1917, he traveled in disguise to the town of Deraa, deep in Ottoman-controlled territory.
sentences.zh: 1917 年底，他乔装打扮前往奥斯曼控制区深处的德拉镇。

sentences.en: He was dressed as an Arab and attempting to gather intelligence when he was captured by Ottoman forces and brought before the local governor, Hajim Bey.
sentences.zh: 他穿着阿拉伯人的衣服试图搜集情报，结果被奥斯曼军队抓获，并被带到当地总督 Hajim Bey 面前。

sentences.en: In his own account, Lawrence wrote that he was beaten, tortured, and sexually assaulted by his captors.
sentences.zh: 在他自己的叙述中，Lawrence 写道他遭到了抓捕者的殴打、酷刑和性侵犯。

sentences.en: He was eventually released, most probably because he never revealed his true identity.
sentences.zh: 他最终获释，很可能是因为他从未透露过自己的真实身份。

sentences.en: Had he done so, and had he been unmasked as the notorious “El Aurens,” as the Arabs called him, he would almost certainly have been shot.
sentences.zh: 如果他透露了身份，或者被揭穿是阿拉伯人所称的那个臭名昭著的“El Aurens”，他几乎肯定会被枪毙。

sentences.en: Now, this makes for a great story, and it is a particularly good part of the movie, but its truth is somewhat debated.
sentences.zh: 这是一个精彩的故事，也是电影中特别出彩的一部分，但其真实性在某种程度上存在争议。

sentences.en: The only account of it comes from Lawrence himself, and he was prone to exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 唯一的叙述来自 Lawrence 本人，而他往往喜欢夸大其词。

sentences.en: What really happened, if anything, will most likely never be known.
sentences.zh: 究竟发生了什么（如果真的发生了什么的话），很可能永远无法知晓。

sentences.en: But what is clear is that something changed in Lawrence after Deraa.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，德拉事件之后，Lawrence 发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: He became more ruthless in battle. He authorised brutal reprisals against Ottoman troops, including the execution of prisoners.
sentences.zh: 他在战斗中变得更加冷酷无情。他授权对奥斯曼军队进行残暴的报复，包括处决战俘。

sentences.en: Some of his Arab allies noticed the shift—he was no longer just a strategist and diplomat.
sentences.zh: 他的一些阿拉伯盟友注意到了这种转变——他不再仅仅是一个战略家和外交官。

sentences.en: He was a man who had been broken and rebuilt by war.
sentences.zh: 他是一个被战争摧毁又重塑的人。

sentences.en: By 1918, Arab forces, alongside the British, reached Damascus.
sentences.zh: 到 1918 年，阿拉伯军队与英军一起抵达了大马士革。

sentences.en: The Ottomans were in retreat. Lawrence rode into the city alongside Faisal’s men.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼人正在撤退。Lawrence 与 Prince Faisal 的部下一起骑马进入了城市。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be the moment of Arab independence.
sentences.zh: 这本该是阿拉伯独立的时刻。

sentences.en: It was not. While Lawrence had been fighting in the desert, diplomats in London and Paris had already divided the Middle East without any consultation of any of its leaders.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。当 Lawrence 在沙漠中战斗时，伦敦和巴黎的外交官们已经在没有咨询任何当地领导人的情况下瓜分了中东。

sentences.en: This was a secret deal signed in 1916, the Sykes-Picot Agreement, in which the British and the French carved up the region after the inevitable fall of the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 这是 1916 年签署的一项秘密协议，即 Sykes-Picot Agreement，英国和法国在其中瓜分了奥斯曼帝国必然垮台后的该地区。

sentences.en: The French would take Syria and Lebanon, while Britain would control Iraq, Jordan, and Palestine.
sentences.zh: 法国将占领叙利亚和黎巴嫩，而英国将控制伊拉克、约旦和巴勒斯坦。

sentences.en: Arab independence was never part of the deal.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯独立从未包含在协议中。

sentences.en: Now, here’s where it gets a little more complicated for T.E.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于 T.E. 来说，情况变得有点复杂了。

sentences.en: Lawrence, the supposed flag carrier and chief proponent of an Arab liberation movement.
sentences.zh: Lawrence，这位所谓的阿拉伯解放运动的旗手和主要支持者。

sentences.en: Lawrence knew about the Sykes-Picot Agreement.
sentences.zh: Lawrence 知道 Sykes-Picot Agreement。

sentences.en: It’s not clear exactly how much he knew, perhaps not all the details, but it's highly likely that he knew of its existence.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚他到底知道多少，也许不是全部细节，但他极有可能知道它的存在。

sentences.en: While apparently promising Prince Faisal one thing, and earning his deep trust and respect, he knew that politicians back in London and Paris had no plans of honouring this agreement.
sentences.zh: 虽然他表面上向 Prince Faisal 承诺了一件事，并赢得了他深厚的信任和尊重，但他知道伦敦和巴黎的政客们根本没有打算履行这一协议。

sentences.en: The promises in the exchange of letters had been kept deliberately vague on the part of the British, giving the Arabs the idea that they were firm promises but leaving room for the British to hold up their hands later on and say “oh no, no, that’s not at all what we meant”.
sentences.zh: 英国人在往来信件中的承诺被刻意保持模糊，让阿拉伯人觉得那是坚定的承诺，但又为英国人日后摊手说“哦不，不，我们根本不是那个意思”留下了余地。

sentences.en: The Arabs were to be used, plain and simple, and once they had done their job and caused enough disruption to the Ottomans, they would be discarded.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，阿拉伯人就是被利用的工具，一旦他们完成了任务，对奥斯曼人造成了足够的破坏，就会被抛弃。

sentences.en: Now, although Lawrence knew about this, it seems that he had tried to ignore it.
sentences.zh: 虽然 Lawrence 知道这一点，但他似乎曾试图忽视它。

sentences.en: Perhaps he hoped that by the time the war ended, and it was clear how important this Arab revolt had been, Britain would have no choice but to honour its promises to the Arabs.
sentences.zh: 也许他希望到战争结束时，当阿拉伯起义的重要性显而易见时，英国将别无选择，只能履行对阿拉伯人的承诺。

sentences.en: But things did not turn out that way. When Damascus fell, Faisal was declared king of Syria—but the French soon removed him by force.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。大马士革陷落后，Prince Faisal 被宣布为叙利亚国王，但法国人很快就用武力罢免了他。

sentences.en: The Arab kingdom Lawrence had fought for vanished almost immediately.
sentences.zh: Lawrence 为之奋斗的阿拉伯王国几乎立即消失了。

sentences.en: He was devastated. He returned to Britain a broken man.
sentences.zh: 他彻底崩溃了。他回到英国时已心灰意冷。

sentences.en: He refused a knighthood, turned down honours, and withdrew from public life.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了爵位，谢绝了荣誉，并退出了公众生活。

sentences.en: He changed his name, enlisted in the Royal Air Force under a false identity, and lived the rest of his life in a self-imposed exile in a 60-metre square cottage in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 他改了名字，以假身份加入英国皇家空军，并在乡下一间 60 平方米的小屋里过着自我放逐的生活。

sentences.en: In 1935, at the age of 46, he died in a motorcycle accident.
sentences.zh: 1935 年，46 岁的他死于一场摩托车事故。

sentences.en: Some say he was running from the past, from the weight of broken promises.
sentences.zh: 有人说他在逃避过去，逃避背弃承诺带来的沉重负担。

sentences.en: Others see him as a tragic figure, a man who tried to shape history but was ultimately powerless against the forces of empire and diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则将他视为一个悲剧人物，一个试图塑造历史，但在帝国和外交力量面前最终无能为力的人。

sentences.en: And the Middle East he left behind, to state the obvious, was not the one he had envisioned.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，他留下的中东并不是他所设想的那个。

sentences.en: The borders drawn by Sykes and Picot still shape the region today.
sentences.zh: Sykes 和 Picot 划定的边界至今仍影响着该地区。

sentences.en: The struggle for Arab independence continued for decades, and resentment towards Western involvement never faded.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯独立的斗争持续了数十年，对西方干预的怨恨从未消退。

sentences.en: To this day, T.E. Lawrence is remembered in different ways.
sentences.zh: 时至今日，人们以不同的方式纪念 T.E. Lawrence。

sentences.en: In Britain, to most he is a romantic figure, a daring adventurer.
sentences.zh: 在英国，对大多数人来说，他是一个浪漫的人物，一个大胆的冒险家。

sentences.en: In the Arab world, he is a more ambiguous symbol—to some, a hero who fought for Arab independence; to others, a man who, knowingly or not, played a role in one of the greatest betrayals of the modern Middle East.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉伯世界，他是一个更具争议的象征——对一些人来说，他是为阿拉伯独立而战的英雄；对另一些人来说，他是一个无论有意还是无意，都在现代中东最伟大的背叛之一中扮演了角色的人。

sentences.en: He is nothing if not impressive, and to end this episode, I will leave you with a quote from the man which I think sums up his sense of adventure.
sentences.zh: 他确实令人印象深刻。在这一集的最后，我将引用他的一句话，我认为这句话总结了他的冒险精神。

sentences.en: “All men dream, but not equally. Those who dream by night in the dusty recesses of their minds wake up in the day to find it was vanity, but the dreamers of the day are dangerous men, for they may act their dreams with open eyes, to make it possible.”
sentences.zh: “所有人都会做梦，但各不相同。那些在夜晚、在脑海幽暗角落做梦的人，白天醒来发现那只是虚幻；但那些在白天做梦的人是危险的，因为他们会睁着眼睛去实践梦想，使其成为可能。”

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on T.E.
sentences.zh: 好了，以上就是今天关于 T.E. 的全部内容。

sentences.en: Lawrence, otherwise known as Lawrence of Arabia.
sentences.zh: Lawrence，也就是众所周知的 Lawrence of Arabia。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 我希望这一集很有趣，并且你学到了一些新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought about this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这一集的看法。

sentences.en: We have lots of listeners from all over the Middle East, so tell me, what do you know and think about this man?
sentences.zh: 我们有很多来自中东各地的听众，所以请告诉我，你对这个人了解多少，怎么看他？

sentences.en: Hero, villain, or somewhere in the middle?
sentences.zh: 英雄、恶棍，还是介于两者之间？

sentences.en: I would love to know, so if you’re listening to this somewhere you can leave a comment, like Spotify or YouTube, then now’s the time to get doing that.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，所以如果你在 Spotify 或 YouTube 等可以留言的地方收听，现在就请留言吧。

sentences.en: Or for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你是我们的会员，可以直接前往我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他求知欲强的朋友们交流。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 推出的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你平安，我们下期再见。
